body: If the tab separation is odd, it will move 1px left or right when dragging over the prev and next tabs. One of these can use ceil, or add 1 to it, so it stays the same.
I think this changes the behavior when over non-equal sized tabs, since you removed the `get_tab_idx_at_point` check.
Thats a good point. I think before it would have prioritized the late-indexed tabs, so I'll re-add the `get_tab_idx_at_point` to account for that.

There's an issue with the hover preview, I think since it now gets the hovered tab first, not always the closest one.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5095d7f-239d-41f0-8b00-94f18f2ab3eb

I'm having some trouble recreating this specific issue (I did notice a similar one where the hover still showed a phantom tab off the end of the tabbar, looking into that). What settings/files are you using? Edit: I think I found it

Found it. Having `get_closest_tab_idx_to_point` call `get_tab_idx_at_point` caused the issue bc `get_tab_idx_at_point` still looked at the rects of hidden tabs, which should not be happening. I modified `get_tab_idx_at_point` to only check tabs that are not hidden, and that fixed the issue.

This isn't an issue with your changes, but this line should be before all the continues. It should run on all tabs, since it needs to be triggered on a tab when it is hidden or just moved, judging by the code in `NOTIFICATION_ACCESSIBILITY_UPDATE`.
If you don't want to change it in this PR, I can open a separate PR for it.
I can do it in this PR, I need to rename the commit anywho.
@kitbdev Looks good? I moved it to line 1156, above both of the early continues. Just curious, how might I test something like this without a screen-reader?
I don't think you can test it without a screen reader. Looks good, I tested it and the behavior is better than before.
